chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Wahb ibn Hafth from Abi Basir who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who prostrates on the leather sock (al-misah), so he said: 'If it is due to taqiya (piety/concealment), there is no harm in it.'

key_terms.الْمِسْحِ: The leather sock worn over the foot for dry ablution (tayammum) or prayer
key_terms.تَقِيَّةٍ: Taqiya; precaution, concealment, or piety, often referring to concealing one's status or actions to avoid harm or for religious precaution

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to prostrate on the leather sock (misah) during prayer if done for taqiya?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence by permitting prostration on the *misah* (leather sock) specifically when motivated by *taqiya* (precautionary concealment), a context often linked to the era of the Imams' political vulnerability. While the primary ruling focuses on the validity of the act under duress or precaution, it underscores the principle that external forms of worship can adapt to internal circumstances of safety and social pressure. This reflects the broader Shia scholarly view that *taqiya* is not merely hiding faith but can validate specific ritual actions that might otherwise be discouraged or require specific conditions.
